info.description: biffix control-plane API (axum + utoipa) — submit, read, ingest, health.

503.description: the deploy configures no OAuth client; the body names the unset variables

get.summary:
`GET /data-sources` — where inputs can be picked from in a project (the default one unless
`project` names another), its bucket first.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
The project whose sources to use (its bucket is the `project` source); absent ⇒ the
deploy's default project. A deploy of one project uses it whatever this names.

post.summary: `POST /data/download-url` — a short-lived URL downloading a file as an attachment.

`POST /data/find` — files under a folder, at any depth, whose name contains `q`. `truncated`
when a match was left out: more than `limit` matched, or the search stopped at its scan budget
before reading the whole folder. The query is in the body, so no folder name or search text
reaches a request URL.

400.description: a cursor S3 did not issue, or an unknown project

post.summary:
`POST /data/head` — whether each pasted or imported path exists (and its size). A URI no data
source shows ([`DataSource::shows`]: outside every source, a folder, or under a prefix biffix
hides) is reported as unknown, not absent: biffix cannot say, a run's role might.

`POST /data/list` — one folder of a data source: its sub-folders and files, a page at a time.
The query is in the body, so no folder name reaches a request URL.

400.description: a cursor S3 did not issue, or an unknown project

post.summary:
`POST /data/preview` — the start of a file as text (gzip/bgzip decompressed), read by the
backend; a binary file comes back as `kind: binary`. The file is named in the body, so no file
name reaches a request URL.

`POST /data/uploads` — start an upload; the response says how to split the file. 409 when an
object already exists at the key: uploads never replace one.

409.description: an object already exists at the key; choose another name

post.summary:
`POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/abort` — cancel an upload; S3 deletes its parts. The key is in
the body, so no file name reaches a request URL.

`POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/complete` — assemble the file from its parts (every part, in
order, with the ETag S3 returned for it). 409 when an object reached the key since the upload
started: nothing is replaced, and the upload is cancelled (upload the file under another name).

409.description: an object already exists at the key; choose another name

post.summary: `POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/parts` — presigned `PUT` URLs for parts (at most 100 at a time).

`POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/status` — the parts already uploaded, so a reload can resume.
The key is in the body, so no file name reaches a request URL.

`POST /data/view-url` — a short-lived URL showing an image, PDF or HTML file inline, its
content type set from its name. 409 for a file with no such viewer.

409.description: the file cannot be shown in the browser; download it

get.summary: The engines biffix runs and the releases a workflow version may pin.

post.summary: Append engine-reported RunEvents for one run.

202.description: the batch landed, but for the events in `refused` (a task_submitted claiming a Batch job the run cannot be shown to own, or whose ts lies outside the job's lifetime)

400.description: malformed batch: an event without a run id, a known kind with a malformed body, a kind no engine may send, or a value the log cannot store (a NUL in text)

403.description: token does not authorize the run these events claim, or the run is cancelled (token revoked)

get.summary:
List experiments, newest activity first: the later of the newest run's submit and the
experiment's creation ([`ExperimentRecord::activity_micros`]), ties by id. `?mine=true` keeps
the caller's: those they created or submitted a run into. Each carries whether it is the
caller's (`mine`) and how many of the caller's runs in it need their attention.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: `true`: only the caller's experiments: those they created or submitted a run into.

post.summary: Create an experiment in a project (one a registered workflow is in).

404.description: no registered workflow is in the project

409.description: the project already has a live experiment of that name

get.summary:
One experiment with its newest runs (newest first, at most [`MAX_DETAIL_RUNS`]), the samples
across those runs, and the summed cost of all of its runs. A bounded read whatever the
experiment's size: its run count and newest run (one aggregate), one page of runs (no count),
that page's per-run costs (one grouped read, as the run list's), their sample facts, and one
cost aggregate.

put.summary: Rename, describe, archive or restore an experiment (a partial update).

409.description: the project already has a live experiment of that name

get.summary: Every sample of every run in an experiment, as a CSV file for a spreadsheet.
get.description:
One row per sample per run (a sample in several runs has a row in each), runs oldest first and
each run's samples in its samples grid's order. Unlike the experiment's detail, which holds only
its newest runs, this reads all of them; it is read on asking, not polled. A run that names no
sample yet (no samplesheet and no task matched to a sample, such as one still preparing its
images) has no rows.

Columns: Sample; Sample status (Waiting, Running, Done, Failed or Stopped); Reused (`yes` when
the sample finished in that run and every one of its steps there came from an earlier run's
results, an engine cache hit or carried from the run it resumed; else `no`); Analysis (the run's
name as the UI shows it: its own, else `<pipeline> · <start> · <N samples>`, the start time in
the time zone `tz` the UI sends, else UTC); Run ID; Analysis status (the run's state in
words: Preparing images, Submitted, Running, Succeeded, Failed or Cancelled); Pipeline; Pipeline
version; Engine; Submitted by; Submitted (UTC) and Finished (UTC), as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

UTF-8 with a byte-order mark (for Excel), CRLF line ends and RFC 4180 quoting. A cell a
spreadsheet could run as a formula gets a leading `'`: one that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`
or their full-width forms after any leading whitespace, or with a tab or line break (numbers
such as `-5` included). So does a cell that already starts with `'`, so a program reading the
file gets every original value back by removing one leading `'` from each cell that has one.

One download covers at most 1,000 runs, about 5 MiB of CSV and 20 s of reading. Past any of
these the answer is a 413 whose message says which limit and what to do, never a file cut short.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description:
The downloader's time zone, an IANA name (`America/New_York`), for the start times in
unnamed analyses' names: each read with the zone's rules for that instant, daylight saving
included, as the UI shows it. Absent or blank: UTC. A name the server does not know is a
400.

200.description: One row per sample per run, with a header row

413.description: Too much to download at once (too many runs, too large a file, or too slow to read); the message says which and what to do

get.summary: Liveness — the process is up. Always 200 if we can serve.

post.summary:
Dismiss some of the caller's failed runs from their *Needs attention*: `run_ids` (1 to 500,
else 400), exactly the runs the caller was shown (one row, or the rows on screen), never an
"everything up to now" cutoff that could take one they have not seen. Runs that are not the
caller's, or did not fail, are ignored. Idempotent; durable and per user
(`notification_dismissals`, recorded `via: dismiss`). Reading a notification is separate: this
neither reads it nor is undone by reading it. Returns how many still need attention; once the
dismissal is recorded it is a 200 even if that count cannot be read (`attention` is then
absent), so a client never shows a recorded dismissal as refused.

get.summary:
The caller's newest notifications (their runs that ended, newest first, at most `limit`:
default 20, clamped to 1..=100), each with whether they have read it, and how many of all theirs
are unread.

post.summary:
Mark some of the caller's notifications read: `ids`, every notification of `run_ids`, or
`all: true` (exactly one, and at most 500 ids, else 400). Ids and runs that are not the
caller's are ignored. Returns the caller's unread counts after.

get.summary: Read the caller's preferences (the defaults when they have none stored).

put.summary:
Update the caller's preferences. A partial update: a field the body leaves out keeps its
stored value. `pin` and `unpin` change one (trimmed) key against the stored list atomically; at
most one of them per body (400), and a pin past the cap is a 400 naming it. An unknown `view`
is a body the API cannot read (422).

get.summary:
`GET /projects` — the deploy's projects: where a workflow version can be registered (each has
its own bucket, roles and data sources), the default first among equals.
Readiness — dependencies reachable (the projection store answers).

`GET /references` — reference bundles, by id; `kind` and `keys` narrow them to the ones a form
can use.

parameters.name: keys
parameters.description: Only bundles with all these keys (comma-separated).

post.summary: `POST /references` — add a bundle (admin). 409 when the id is taken.

put.summary:
`PUT /references/{id}` — replace a bundle's contents (admin). Runs already launched keep the
URIs they used (their anchors record them). The bundle keeps who created it and when.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /references/{id}` — remove a bundle (admin). Forms stop offering it; runs launched with
it keep their record.

get.summary: List runs, filterable by state, searchable, and paginated.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Which runs by state (default all). A string here, parsed with `RunFilter::parse` once the
caller may list runs: an unknown one is a 400.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text search: a case-insensitive substring of one of run id, run name, workflow name,
the pipeline's title (its form's `title`), workflow-version id, submitter, submitter label,
project or engine. A name the UI derives for an unnamed run is not searched as a whole, but
its pipeline title is.

parameters.name: workflow
parameters.description: Exact frozen workflow-version id to scope to (runs of one registered version).

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: `true`: only runs the caller submitted ("my runs"). Default: everyone's.

parameters.name: attention
parameters.description:
`true`: only the caller's failed runs they have not dismissed (the Lab home's *Needs
attention*; opening or reading one leaves it there). Implies `mine`.

parameters.name: experiment
parameters.description: Only the runs in this experiment.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, clamped by the store).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: return the next (older) page after this one. From a prior `last_cursor`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: return the previous (newer) page. From a prior `first_cursor`.

post.summary: Submit a run.
post.description:
503 when AWS or the store is unavailable (retry), or when the deploy has no capability secret,
so no run can launch.

post.summary:
`POST /runs/query` — `GET /runs` with its parameters in a JSON body, the form the UI uses: the
search text can be a run name, which can name a sample, and a body is not logged the way a
request URL is. Same answers.

get.summary: Get one run's detail (status + task table).

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description:
`false` leaves out the task table (an empty `tasks`): a client that pages tasks through
`POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query` polls the run without re-fetching every task. Default `true`.

post.summary:
`POST /runs/{run_id}/attempts/query` — every AWS Batch attempt of one task (e.g. a
spot-reclaimed attempt and its successful retry), each with its own exit code, reason, log
stream and host. Empty for a task that never became a Batch job (a local rule, a cache hit). The
task key rides in a JSON body: it names a sample, and must not reach a request URL.

Cancel a run: record who asked (`cancel_requested`, which makes a failure terminal stamped after
it fold to CANCELLED), then terminate its coordinator Batch job and its live task jobs.
The engine does not reliably stop its children when its head job is terminated (Nextflow leaves
them running), so the children are terminated here too, best-effort and concurrently; the
reconcile Lambda's ended-run sweep terminates any that remain — so cancel stops the spend, not
just the tracking.
post.description:
A run with no coordinator yet (one waiting for its submit-time images) may be one the launch
sweep is launching at this moment, so its cancel takes the run's launch claim first (waiting up
to 20 s for a launch in progress, else 503: retry), and re-reads the run under it: a
coordinator bound meanwhile is stopped as any other; otherwise the run ends and its parked
launch is dropped while the claim is held, so no sweep launches it after.

A run not yet confirmed running (`submitted`) is also marked cancelled (`run_cancelled`): its
coordinator may never have started (or never will report), so no terminal would otherwise
arrive. That terminal is recorded only once the coordinator's terminate succeeded (or there is
no coordinator to terminate), so a run is never shown cancelled while its coordinator may still
start. An already finished run is an idempotent no-op. If terminating the coordinator fails, the
request stays recorded but the run is not ended, and the call returns 502 so the caller knows
the run may still be running; a retry re-attempts the terminate.

502.description: the cancel is recorded, but terminating the coordinator failed; retry

503.description: the run is being launched; retry

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/coordinator-logs` — a page of the run's coordinator (workflow driver) log,
served through biffix like task logs. Where a run that failed before scheduling any task (clone,
staging, or DAG errors) explains itself. Empty page when no stream was recorded: the coordinator
has not started, or the run predates coordinator log tracking.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque CloudWatch cursor from a prior page.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description:
`forward` (from the given cursor toward newer events, or from the start of the stream when
no cursor is given) or `backward`/absent (tail — newest first).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max events to return (default 200, clamped to 1..=1000).

post.summary:
Put a run in an experiment of its project, move it to another, or take it out (`null`, or a
blank id). The body must name `experiment_id` (a 400 otherwise, so a misspelled field is not
read as "take it out"). Recorded as the run's `experiment_set` event; returns the run's summary
after.

400.description: no `experiment_id` in the body, the run has no project, or the experiment is archived or in another project

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/failure-summary` — why a failed run failed, in plain words: its first failed
steps (earliest first), each with its cause, what to try, and the end of its log; or the workflow
engine's own failure when no step failed. Empty for a run that did not fail.

post.summary:
Rename a run, or clear its name (`null`, or a blank name) so readers show a derived one. Allowed
to whoever may control the run, as for cancelling it or moving it between experiments
(`LaunchWorkflow` on a run they can see). The body must name `run_name` (a 400 otherwise, so a
misspelled field is not read as "clear"). Recorded as the run's `run_renamed` event, so the name
folds into the projection and a replay keeps it; returns the run's summary after.

400.description: no `run_name` in the body, or the name is too long

post.summary:
`POST /runs/{run_id}/outputs/query` — a page of the objects the run registered, ordered by S3
URI. The filters are in a JSON body, so a task key, a directory or a cursor (all of which can
name a sample or a file) never appears in a request URL. An output registered outside the
output prefix is shown by its engine path or bucket key instead and is never under any
`prefix`; the role `*` is every role, including ones this build does not know (the role is an
open enum).

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}` — one output of the run, shaped as in the list. A
client that names an output by id (a link to an open file) can show it without paging through
the whole list to find it. 404 when the id is not an output of this run; a file it reused from
a run it resumed counts as its output.

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/alignment-view` — presigned Range-readable links to a BAM
or CRAM output and its index, the reference to show it against (the run's recorded reference
bundle, or `?reference=`; a bundle's `igv_genome` names a hosted genome instead), and where to
open (the first contig with mapped reads, read from the file's own index and header; skipped
with `?locus=false`, as a client renewing its links does). The links last an hour at most: ask
again before `expires_at`, or when a read is refused. 409 when the output is not a BAM/CRAM or
has no index.

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: A reference bundle id to show the alignment against, instead of the run's own.

parameters.name: locus
parameters.description:
Find where to open (`locus`; default true). `false` skips reading the index and header, for
a client only renewing its links: the response then has no `locus`.

404.description: no such output, or no such reference bundle

409.description: not a BAM or CRAM, or it has no index

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/download` — a short-lived presigned URL that downloads
the object as an attachment. 404 when the id is not an output of this run; 403 when the output
is one biffix does not serve ([`checkable`]).

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/fastqc` — the pipeline's own FastQC result for an
output, as data: the output's `_fastqc.zip` itself, the zip beside a `_fastqc.html`, or, for a
FASTQ, the zip FastQC names after it (`S1_R1.fastq.gz` → `S1_R1_fastqc.zip`) among the run's
registered outputs, when it is unambiguously that FASTQ's. 404 when there is none (the client
falls back to the HTML report); 422 when the zip is too large or not FastQC's.

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

404.description: no FastQC result for this output

422.description: the FastQC zip is too large or unreadable

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/preview` — the start of an output as text, read by the
backend (so it works whatever the bucket's CORS). A gzip/bgzip file is decompressed; a binary
file comes back as `kind: binary` with no text.

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/view-url` — a short-lived URL that shows an image, PDF
or HTML output inline. The content type is set from the file name, never from what S3 stored
(uploads are often `binary/octet-stream`). 409 for an output with no such viewer.

parameters.name: output_id
parameters.description: the output's opaque id (from the list)

409.description: the file cannot be shown in the browser; download it

get.summary: `GET /runs/{run_id}/provenance` — the run's Workflow Run RO-Crate metadata, as a download.

200.description: The run's ro-crate-metadata.json (WRROC 0.6 Provenance Run Crate)

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/qc/fastqc-status` — each FastQC result's module statuses and basic
statistics as MultiQC recorded them, each attributed to the run's sample that owns it: for a
pipeline that publishes MultiQC's output but not FastQC's own zips. Read from every FastQC table
in `multiqc_data/` beside the report `/reports` lists with kind `multiqc` (one per FastQC
section: `multiqc_fastqc.txt`, and `multiqc_fastqc_<anchor>.txt` for a section with an anchor
or a repeated one), each result tagged with its section. 404 when the run has no MultiQC report,
or the report no FastQC table: MultiQC wrote its data in another format (`data_format`, said in
the message), or as `multiqc_data.zip` (`--zip-data-dir`, not read), or ran no FastQC module.

404.description: no MultiQC report, or no FastQC table (TSV) in its data

422.description: MultiQC's FastQC tables are too large to read

get.summary:
`GET /runs/{run_id}/qc/general-stats` — the MultiQC report's General Statistics as data: the
values from `multiqc_data/multiqc_general_stats.txt` beside the report, with the columns'
metadata from `multiqc_data/multiqc_data.json` (plain column names when that is missing). The
report is the one `/reports` lists with kind `multiqc`.
`GET /runs/{run_id}/reports` — the run's reports.

`GET /runs/{run_id}/samples` — the run's samples × steps (the Lab view's per-sample progress):
each sample's state and its cell per step, the whole-study steps, in pipeline order.

post.summary:
`POST /runs/{run_id}/task-logs/query` — a page of one task's CloudWatch log stream, served
through biffix's own auth (ViewRuns) so a scientist needs a biffix login, not an AWS account, to
read why their job failed. The stream is derived server-side from the authorized task; the client
supplies only the run id, task key, and an opaque paging cursor. They ride in a JSON body: the
task key names a sample, and a body is not logged the way a request URL is.

`POST /runs/{run_id}/tasks/query` — one page of the run's tasks, with its filters in a JSON
body: a search term or a task key can name a sample, and a body is not logged the way a request
URL is. 400 for an unknown `state`, `sort` or `order` (checked only once the caller may see the
run, so a bad parameter never tells an unauthorized caller anything).
Group files into samples.

400.description: a bad regular expression, or too many files

413.description: the request body is over 6 MiB

get.summary: Read the site settings (title + logo). Viewer-gated; every page fetches it for its chrome.

put.summary:
Update the site settings. Developer-gated (same capability as registering a workflow); a body
that sets or clears the support contact also needs an Admin ([`Capability::ManageSupportContact`]).
put.description:
A partial update: a field the body leaves out keeps its stored value; `null` or an empty (for
the title, blank) string clears it.

requestBody.description: absent field: keep; null or empty: clear

get.summary: List the operational-alert recipients. Developer-gated, like editing settings.

post.summary:
Add an alert recipient. AWS emails it a confirmation link; it receives alerts once confirmed.
Adding an address that is already subscribed is a no-op.

Remove a confirmed alert recipient. A pending one cannot be removed (SNS has no id for it until
it is confirmed); it lapses on its own after 3 days unconfirmed. The address is in the body,
keeping it out of the request URL, where access logs keep it.

get.summary:
The service-status page data. Reads ONLY Postgres: a live `SELECT 1` for the database plus the
latest probe sample per component (the reconcile lambda does the AWS calls and writes samples).
A stale sample is escalated — the probe not reporting is itself a fault.
Bucketed uptime history for the status bars, from the probe's `status_samples`.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: `1h`, `1d`, `1w` or `90d` (default): selects both the span and the bucket size.

503.description: the status samples could not be read

get.summary: Estimated spend of the runs submitted in a period, grouped, with the period's total.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (default: the first of this month).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The day after the period, `YYYY-MM-DD` (default: the first of next month).

get.summary: List registered workflow versions (newest first), each saying whether it is released.

parameters.name: released
parameters.description:
Only released (`true`) or only developer (`false`) versions; absent: every version. A value
other than `true`/`false` is a 400.

503.description: the registry, or the versions' release state, could not be read

post.summary: Register (freeze) an immutable workflow version.

201.description: Registered, and it can run already

202.description: Registered; its runtime or images are still being built

put.summary:
Hide a workflow from the Lab's pipeline cards, or show it again. Applies to every version of
the (project, name); the Expert list still shows a hidden one. Developer-gated, like
registering. The name travels in the body since it may contain `/`.

404.description: no registered version has that project and name

post.summary:
Presign a PUT for staging a workflow-source tarball: an S3-staged source, which is how a
workflow in a private repository is registered. Developer-gated. The client PUTs the tarball to
the returned URL, then calls `POST /workflows` with `source = {kind:s3, uri}`, which checks
again that the URI stays inside the staging area of the version's project bucket. `project`
picks the bucket; one this deploy does not configure is a 400.

get.summary:
Fetch one registered version by its frozen id, including its `form_schema`. Viewer-gated, like
the other reads. The list view omits `form_schema`, so the CLI needs this to
validate submit params against the registered schema.

503.description: the version, or its release state, could not be read

get.summary:
`GET /workflows/{id}/estimate?samples=N` — what a launch of this workflow with N samples may
cost and how long it may take, from the workflow's recent successful runs (any version, same
project and name). No estimate until two such runs recorded a cost and a sample count. `typical`
is one run of it, whatever its sample count (a running analysis's ETA, a catalog card's "usually
~2 h"): from two successful runs.

parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Samples the launch is for; absent (or 0) asks for the typical run only.

post.summary:
Import a version's image again after its automatic imports failed. Developer-gated, like
registration. An image that is imported or importing is left as it is.

put.summary:
Release a version, or (`released: false`) un-release it so it is a developer version again.
Developer-gated, like registering. Recorded with who and when, and kept: the response's
`history` lists every change. Releasing a released version (or un-releasing a developer one)
changes nothing and records nothing.

post.summary:
Register a version again from what it recorded: on this deploy's engine runtime (or the exact
`engine_version` given), with its images pinned again, in its project (or the `project` given).
Developer-gated, like registration. The same inputs as an existing build of the source are a 409
naming it; `dry_run` reports what would be registered and writes nothing.

Build a version's coordinator variant again after its automatic builds failed (e.g. once a
transient upstream outage has passed). Developer-gated, like registration. A variant that is
ready or building is left as it is; the response is its state either way.

AlertRecipient.description: One email that receives operational alerts.

status.description: `confirmed`, or `pending` until the recipient clicks the link in AWS's confirmation email.

AlertRecipientList.description:
`GET /settings/alerts` — the alert recipients. `configured` is false when the deploy has no
alerts topic.

AlertRecipientRemoveRequest.description:
`POST /settings/alerts/remove` — remove a recipient. The address travels in the body, not the
request URL, so access logs don't keep it.

AlignmentLinks.description:
What a genome browser needs to show one alignment output
(`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/alignment-view`). Every URL is a presigned GET the
browser reads directly with HTTP Range requests; they stop working at `expires_at` (or sooner,
when the credentials that signed them end), so a client that stays open asks again before
then, and when a read is refused, with `?locus=false` (only the links change).

expires_at.description: Epoch seconds after which the URLs no longer work.

locus.description:
Where to open: the first contig with mapped reads, as `name:start-end` (1-based, inclusive),
when the file's index and its own header say. `None` ⇒ the browser's own default (and
always with `?locus=false`).

notes.description:
Why something is missing or was left out (an annotation too large to load unindexed, a
reference file outside every data source, …), for the viewer to show.

oneOf.description:
The reference to show it against; `None` when the run recorded no reference bundle and none
was asked for (the client offers a choice).
The bundle's FASTA, through presigned URLs.
The bundle's gene annotation, when it can be loaded.
A genome the browser hosts, by its id (`hg38`, `mm39`).

AlignmentReference.description:
The reference an alignment is shown against: a bundle's own FASTA (and annotation), or a genome
the genome browser hosts (the bundle's `igv_genome`), which sends the browser to that host.

AlignmentTrack.description: The alignment file and its index.

index_url.description: The tabix index of a bgzipped annotation; `None` ⇒ the whole (small) file is loaded.

AttentionCount.description: The reply to a dismissal: how many of the caller's runs still need their attention.

attention.description: Absent when the dismissal was recorded but the count could not be read afterwards.

AttentionDismissRequest.description:
`POST /me/attention/dismiss` — take some of the caller's failed runs out of their *Needs
attention* (one row's Dismiss, or *Dismiss all* naming exactly the runs it shows). Opening a run
or reading its notification does not; this does, as trying the run again does.

run_ids.description:
The runs to dismiss (1 to 500). A run that is not the caller's, or does not need their
attention, is ignored.

CarriedCoverage.description: A sample from before a [`StatusHistory`] window, as far as it covers the window.

CatalogEntry.description:
A version's entry in the Lab's pipeline catalog (`catalog:` in `biffix.yaml`, frozen with the
form).

oneOf.description:
Who to ask about this workflow's runs (the author's `catalog.contact`); wins over the site's
support contact.

description.description:
The card's description: the catalog's, else the form's, else the About page's first
sentence.

inputs.description:
What a run takes: the launch form's main inputs in plain words (its samplesheet and file
inputs a launch must give, and its reference dropdown), in form order.

results.description:
What a run gives you: the names of the key results the version declares (`reports:` in
`biffix.yaml`), in declaration order, each once.

tags.description: Tags to filter on (normalized at registration: trimmed, unique ignoring case).

verified.description: The author vouches for the workflow.

ComponentHistory.description: One component's uptime history within a [`StatusHistory`], buckets in time order.

oneOf.description:
The newest sample before the window, when its promise (plus the grace) may reach into it:
what covers the window's start until its first sample (an idle tenant samples hourly).

CostByInstanceType.description: The estimate grouped by the host type (and lifecycle) the jobs ran on.

DagNode.description: A node in the run's group-level DAG, with its task-instance state rollup.

DataFile.description: An object in a listing or a search.

path.description: Its path relative to the source root.

viewer.description:
How the browser can show it, from its name (`table`, `text`, `image`, `pdf`, `html`), as for
run outputs; absent when it can only be downloaded.

DataFileRequest.description:
`POST /data/preview`, `/data/view-url` and `/data/download-url` request: one file of a source,
named in the body rather than the request URL.

path.description: The file, relative to the source root.

project.description:
The project whose sources to use (its bucket is the `project` source); absent ⇒ the
deploy's default project. A deploy of one project uses it whatever this names.

The project whose sources to use (its bucket is the `project` source); absent ⇒ the
deploy's default project. A deploy of one project uses it whatever this names.

q.description: A fragment of the file name (case-insensitive).

DataFindResult.description: `POST /data/find`: objects under a folder (at any depth) whose name contains a fragment.

truncated.description:
A match may have been left out: more files matched than the limit, or the search stopped
at its scan budget before reading the whole folder.

path.description: Its path relative to the source root, ending in `/`.

DataFolderPage.description: `POST /data/list`: one folder of a data source, one page at a time.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last.

path.description: The folder listed, relative to the source root (`""` for the root, else ending in `/`).

exists.description:
`true` exists; `false` absent; absent when the URI is outside every data source (biffix
cannot see it, but a run's role might).

DataHeadRequest.description: `POST /data/head` request: which objects to look up.

project.description:
The project whose sources to use (its bucket is the `project` source); absent ⇒ the
deploy's default project. A deploy of one project uses it whatever this names.

DataListRequest.description:
`POST /data/list` request: in a body, so folder names (which can name samples) never reach a
request URL or an access log.

path.description: The folder, relative to the source root.

project.description:
The project whose sources to use (its bucket is the `project` source); absent ⇒ the
deploy's default project. A deploy of one project uses it whatever this names.

starts_with.description: Only names in the folder that start with this.

DataSource.description:
A place a run's inputs can come from: the project's own bucket, or an S3 location an admin
registered in the deploy config (a sequencing core's drop folder, a reference library).

browsable_exceptions.description:
Paths under a `hidden_prefixes` entry that are browsable after all (a project's run
folders, `biffix/runs/`).

hidden_prefixes.description:
Paths (relative to the root) the Data page hides: a folder or file whose path starts with
one of these cannot be listed, previewed or downloaded through the source, unless its path
also starts with one of `browsable_exceptions`. The server's own rule, so a client can tell
whether a link into the source would open rather than copy it. Empty (absent) when the
source hides nothing.

id.description: Stable id (`project` for the project bucket).

name.description: The name people know it by ("Sequencing core drop").

writable.description:
Files can be uploaded here: the project bucket, when the deploy has enabled browser uploads
to it (its CORS rule is in place).

EngineSupport.description:
`GET /engines` — an engine biffix runs and the releases a workflow version may pin as its
`engine_version`: an exact release from `min_version` (inclusive) to `below_version`
(exclusive), written the way the engine writes its versions — and, when `releases` is given,
one of those (the only releases biffix can build; Nextflow's are pinned by sha256).

Experiment.description: One experiment, with a summary of its runs.

archived_at.description: Set once archived (hidden from the default list); epoch seconds.

created_by.description: Who created it (their id), and how to show them.

last_run_at.description: When its newest run was submitted (epoch seconds).

mine.description:
Whether it is the caller's: they created it, or submitted a run into it (what `?mine=true`
keeps). Per caller, so a list of everyone's can be split into Mine and All without a second
read.

needs_attention.description:
How many of the caller's own runs in it need their attention: failed, and not dismissed
from their *Needs attention* (as the run list's `?attention=true` reads it). Per caller; 0 for one
with no runs in it.

project.description: The project it lives in (its runs are this project's).

run_count.description: How many runs are in it.

ExperimentCreateRequest.description:
`POST /experiments` — create one. The name is trimmed, 1..=200 characters, unique (ignoring
case) among the project's experiments that are not archived.

ExperimentDetail.description:
`GET /experiments/{id}` — the experiment, its newest runs (newest first, at most 200), the
samples across those runs and one total cost over all of its runs.

runs.description:
Its newest runs, newest first: all of them up to 200, else the 200 newest (see
`runs_total`; the run list's `?experiment=` pages through every one).

runs_total.description: How many runs it holds in all (`runs.len()` unless the list was cut short).

samples.description: Samples named by any of `runs`, in first-seen order (runs oldest first).

total_cost_usd.description:
The sum of the estimated costs of all of its runs (not only `runs`); absent when none has
a priced job.

ExperimentList.description:
`GET /experiments` — newest activity first: an experiment's activity is the later of its newest
run's submit and its own creation (so a new experiment filled with older runs sorts as new), ties
broken by id. `?project=` scopes to one project; `?archived=true` includes archived ones;
`?mine=true` keeps only the caller's: those they created or submitted a run into (a run in it
whose submitter is them, as the run list's `?mine=true` reads a run's submitter).

ExperimentSample.description:
One sample across an experiment's runs: its state in each run that has it, by run id. A state is
the samples grid's row state for that sample in that run: `waiting`, `running`, `done`, `failed`
or `stopped` (an open set: a client shows one it does not know as is).

ExperimentUpdateRequest.description:
`PUT /experiments/{id}` — a partial update: an absent field keeps its value; `description:
null` (or blank) clears it; `archived` archives (`true`) or restores (`false`).

FailureItem.description: One failed step (or the engine), its cause and what to try.

batch_job_id.description: The AWS Batch job of the failed task's last attempt (for a support report).

cause.description:
`could_not_start`, `out_of_memory`, `spot_reclaimed`, `host_lost`, `timed_out`,
`missing_input`, `bad_input`, `reference_mismatch`, `no_space`, `access_denied`,
`missing_output`, `step_error`, `engine_error`, `launch_failed` or `unknown` (open: a reader
treats a value it does not know as unknown).

exit_code.description:
The exit code of the failed task's last attempt, when AWS recorded one; for a Snakemake job
whose log names its command's own exit status, that status (its job exits 1 whatever the
command did).

log_tail.description: The last lines of its log (or the engine's), oldest first.

reason.description:
AWS's own reason its last attempt stopped, when it gave one (e.g. why a container could not
start — there is no log then); or, when the workflow engine failed a step whose job
succeeded, the engine's reason.

sample.description: The sample the failed task belongs to (per-sample progress), when it is attributed to one.

stage.description:
Set when the run failed before it launched: the control-plane stage it stopped at
(`image_preparation` or `launch`; open, so a reader treats any value as "before launch").
There is then no job or engine log to open. Absent for a failed step or the engine.

step.description: What to call it: the step (rule/process) name, else the task key, else `workflow engine`.

task_key.description: The failed task; absent for the engine's own failure.

try_again.description:
What *Try again* should do for this cause: `resume` (pick up where it stopped), `rerun`
(start again with the same inputs), `fix_samples` or `fix_options` (retrying unchanged would
fail the same way: open the launch form pre-filled at samples / at options). Open.

FailureSummary.description: Why a failed run failed, in plain words (`GET /runs/{id}/failure-summary`).

failed_steps.description: How many steps failed (the items cover the first few).

items.description:
The first failed steps, earliest first; or the engine's own failure when no step failed.
Empty for a run that did not fail.

oneOf.description:
Who to ask about this run: its workflow's `catalog.contact`, else the site's support
contact; `None` when neither is set.

FastqcBasicStats.description: FastQC's basic statistics as MultiQC recorded them (each absent when MultiQC had none).

percent_duplicates.description:
Duplicate reads, a percent (0–100), as MultiQC reports them: 100 − FastQC's total
deduplicated percentage.

poor_quality.description: Reads FastQC flagged as poor quality (FastQC 0.10's `Filtered Sequences`).

FastqcModule.description: One FastQC module (`>>Per base sequence quality\tpass` … `>>END_MODULE`).

columns.description: The table's column names (its last `#` header line, without the `#`).

extra.description:
Header lines before the column names, as `[key, value]` (`["Total Deduplicated
Percentage", "94.08"]`).

name.description: The module's name as FastQC writes it (`Per base sequence quality`).

rows.description:
The table's rows, each cell as written (numbers are not parsed; a cell may be a range such
as `10-14`).

status.description: `pass`, `warn` or `fail` as FastQC wrote it. Open: a later FastQC may write others.

truncated.description:
The module held more than the API returns (more rows, or more cells in a row, than its caps,
or the file's data ran past what one response carries); `rows` holds the first ones.

FastqcModuleStatus.description: One FastQC module's status, without its data.

name.description: The module's name as FastQC writes it (`Per base sequence quality`).

status.description:
`pass`, `warn` or `fail`, in the case MultiQC wrote it (compare case-insensitively). A cell
that is none of these is no module.

FastqcReport.description:
A FastQC result as data (`GET /runs/{run_id}/outputs/{output_id}/fastqc`): the modules of the
`fastqc_data.txt` inside the pipeline's own `_fastqc.zip`.

html_output_id.description:
The FastQC HTML report beside the zip, when the run registered one (open it with the
output's view URL).

modules.description: The modules in the file's order.

output_id.description: The `_fastqc.zip` output the modules were read from.

version.description: The FastQC version that wrote it (`0.12.1`), from the file's first line.

FastqcStatusReport.description:
Per-sample FastQC statuses from the run's MultiQC data (`GET /runs/{run_id}/qc/fastqc-status`):
for a pipeline that publishes MultiQC's output but not FastQC's own `_fastqc.zip`s, which the
FastQC viewer needs. Statuses and basic statistics only: MultiQC's data holds no FastQC plots.

report_output_id.description: The MultiQC report whose data these are (an output of the run; open it for the plots).

samples.description:
One per FastQC result MultiQC read (a paired-end sample has two), section by section (the
unanchored `multiqc_fastqc.txt` first, then each `multiqc_fastqc_<anchor>.txt` by name);
within a section the run's samples first in the run's sample order, then any result no
sample owns, each group by MultiQC name.

source.description:
Where the statuses were read from: `multiqc` (`multiqc_data/multiqc_fastqc.txt`). Open:
other sources may follow.

FastqcStatusSample.description: One FastQC result as MultiQC summarised it.

fastqc_name.description: MultiQC's name for it (usually the FASTQ's name without its extension: `S1_R1`).

filename.description: The FASTQ FastQC read (`S1_R1.fastq.gz`), when MultiQC recorded it.

modules.description: FastQC's modules in MultiQC's column order.

sample.description:
The run's sample this result belongs to: the longest sample id the MultiQC name starts with,
followed by the end or a character that cannot continue an id (`S1_R1` is S1's, `S10_R1`
S10's); when no id owns the MultiQC name (MultiQC renamed, prefixed or truncated it), the
same rule on `filename`'s stem. Ids match literally: one holding `*` or `?` is no glob here.
The rule cannot tell a read suffix from an id: with samples `S1` and `S1_1`, the result
`S1_1` (S1's read 1, as nf-core names reads) is `S1_1`'s. `None` when no sample owns it.

section.description:
The MultiQC FastQC section this result is from, when the report has several (FastQC run on
raw and on trimmed reads): the anchor in its table's name, as written
(`multiqc_fastqc_fastqc_trimmed.txt` → `fastqc_trimmed`; a repeated unanchored section's is
`fastqc-1`). `None` for the unanchored `multiqc_fastqc.txt`. The same MultiQC name can be in
several sections.

HealthStatus.description:
A component's health tier. Explicit (not a `healthy: bool`), so a healthy-but-noisy component can
carry a `detail` without being read as degraded.

Variants are declared worst-last, so the derived `Ord` *is* the severity ordering — rolling
components up to an overall tier is [`HealthStatus::worse`] (a `max`).

Host.description:
The EC2 host an attempt ran on, joined from the ECS host registry, plus whether it was spot or
on-demand. Every field is optional: a host registered before the registry existed has only the
queue-derived capacity, and a still-queued attempt has no host at all.

capacity_source.description:
Where `capacity` came from: `instance` (EC2 reported it for this host) or `queue` (the job
queue's configured capacity, used when the instance's own lifecycle is unknown).

queue.description: The Batch job queue (name) the attempt ran on.

registered_memory_mib.description: Memory (MiB) ECS could allocate on the host, after the agent's reservation.

registered_vcpus.description: vCPUs ECS could allocate on the host.

ImageArchBuild.description: One architecture's build of a built image.

ImageBuildRequest.description:
An image to build from a recipe the workflow ships; its context is staged first
(`POST /workflows/source-upload` with `context_tree_hash`).

context.description:
The context directory in the workflow (`docker/align`; an empty string for the root). For
`pixi`, the environment's directory.

context_uri.description:
The staged context tarball: `s3://<project bucket>/workflow-sources/<source id>/contexts/
<tree_hash>.tar.gz`.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile's path within the context (`dockerfile`).

tree_hash.description: The content hash of the context's files (paths within the context).

ImageRequest.description: One named image in a registration.

oneOf.description: A recipe in the workflow to build the image from.

ref.description:
An image reference to import (`quay.io/biocontainers/fastqc:0.12.1--hdfd78af_0`). Exactly
one of `ref` and `build`.

runtime.description: `own`: a Snakemake image that carries its own Snakemake.

IngestRequest.description:
A batch of engine events. Batched because the plugin buffers, and one POST per event would put a
network round trip in the engine's hot path.

Each element is an engine wire event, kept raw here and parsed one by one, so a kind this backend
does not know yet (a newer plugin's) is stored unfolded instead of failing the whole batch: an
event's kind is an open enum.

appended.description: Events durably appended by this call (excludes duplicates already in the log).

duplicates.description: Events accepted but already present, deduped on `dedup_key`. A plugin retry is a no-op.

refused.description:
Events of the batch the route refused one by one and did not append (a `task_submitted`
whose Batch job claim it could not verify), each with why. The rest of the batch landed; a
resend of a refused event is refused again, so a poster logs it and drops it.

JobCost.description: One job's estimated cost (an attempt, or the coordinator).

price_per_hour.description: The average compute price over the job, USD/hour.

price_source.description:
Where the compute price came from: `on_demand` (list price), `spot_history` (EC2 spot price
history for the host's type and AZ — what spot bills), `spot_at_on_demand` (spot, history
unavailable: an upper bound), `unknown_at_on_demand` (lifecycle unknown).

LaunchEstimate.description: USD for the samples asked for (median, and the 25th–75th percentile range), and median hours.

runs.description: Past runs the estimate is from.

LogLine.description: One log line from a task attempt's CloudWatch stream.

ts_ms.description: Event time, epoch milliseconds (CloudWatch's native unit).

LogPage.description:
`POST /runs/{id}/task-logs/query`: a page of a task's log stream. Serves the logs *through*
biffix (gated by the caller's ViewRuns capability), so viewing a task's logs needs a biffix
login, not an AWS console account. The stream name is derived server-side from the task the caller is
authorized to see — never supplied by the client.

log_stream.description:
The CloudWatch stream these events came from. `None` ⇒ the task has no stream yet (still
queued, a cache-hit, or a local rule that never became a Batch job) — render "no logs yet".

next_forward_token.description:
Opaque CloudWatch cursors — pass one back as `cursor` to page. `next_backward_token` walks
toward older events ("load earlier"); `next_forward_token` toward newer ("live tail").

NextflowPluginRequest.description: One Nextflow plugin a workflow declares, at an exact version.

sha256.description: sha256 (64 lowercase hex) of the plugin registry's `<id>-<version>.zip`.

Notification.description: One notification: a run of the caller's ended (or failed before it launched).

id.description: Stable id (one per run and kind; a replay rebuilds the same id).

kind.description: `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled` (open: a reader shows an unknown kind plainly).

read.description:
The caller has read it (opened the run, marked it read, or tried the run again). Read state is
the bell's alone: a failed run read still needs attention until it is dismissed.

run_name.description: The run's name, when it has one.

samples_total.description:
The run's sample counts when it has per-sample progress, for "12 samples" / "1 sample
failed".

submitted_at.description: When the run was submitted (epoch seconds), when known.

workflow_name.description: The workflow's name (the Lab view calls it the pipeline).

workflow_title.description:
The pipeline's friendly title (its form's `title`), when its author gave one; with
`submitted_at` and the sample count it names a run that has no `run_name`.

NotificationList.description:
`GET /me/notifications` — the caller's latest notifications, newest first, and how many of all
of theirs are unread.

unread_failed.description:
How many of the caller's failed runs are unread (the bell's; *Needs attention* counts the
failed runs not dismissed, as the run list's `attention` filter reads it).

NotificationsReadRequest.description:
`POST /me/notifications/read` — mark some of the caller's notifications read. Give exactly one
of `ids`, `run_ids` (every notification of those runs) or `all: true`.

OAuthClientConfig.description:
`GET /auth/config` — the public OAuth client configuration (no secrets). The CLI reads this to
discover the native client id + registered loopback redirect URIs (no client id is baked in).

cli_client_id.description:
The native CLI app client id, when a CLI client is deployed. Public and
non-secret; the `biffix` CLI discovers it here so no client id is baked into the binary.

cli_redirect_uris.description:
The registered loopback redirect URIs for the CLI client. Cognito matches a
redirect URI exactly, so the CLI must bind one of these registered ports.

logout_endpoint.description:
Cognito's hosted-UI logout endpoint. Ending the IdP session is what makes sign-out real; a
client that only clears its own tokens is silently signed back in on the next request.

logout_uri.description: Where Cognito returns the browser after logout (a registered logout URL).

region.description:
The AWS region the deploy runs in (e.g. `us-west-2`), for deep links into the AWS console
(S3, Batch, CloudWatch). Non-secret. `None` when the backend cannot tell (no `AWS_REGION`).

user_pool_id.description:
The Cognito user pool id, derived from the OIDC issuer. Non-secret (it appears in every
token's issuer), and lets the UI link a run's submitter to the Cognito console. `None` when
the issuer isn't a Cognito issuer (e.g. auth disabled / a local non-Cognito setup).

OutputPrefixKind.description: How a run's output prefix relates to the run.

OutputPreview.description: The start of one output as text (`GET /runs/{id}/outputs/{output_id}/preview`).

decompressed.description: The object was gzip (or bgzip) and `text` is its decompressed start.

kind.description: `text`, or `binary` when the bytes are not text (then `text` is empty).

total_size.description: The object's size, when S3 reported it.

truncated.description: More of the file exists than `text` shows.

OutputUrl.description: A short-lived URL for one output (`GET /runs/{id}/outputs/{output_id}/download`).

content_type.description: The content type the URL serves the object as (view URLs only).

expires_at.description: Epoch seconds after which the URL no longer works.

Project.description:
`GET /projects`: one of the deploy's projects (each has its own bucket, roles and data
sources; a workflow version runs in its own).

default.description: The deploy's default project (where a request naming none goes).

uploads.description: Browsers may upload into the project bucket.

viewer_cors.description: The project bucket allows the alignment viewer's cross-origin reads.

QcColumn.description: One General Statistics column, with MultiQC's display hints.

cond_formatting_rules.description: MultiQC's `{pass|warn|fail: [{gt|lt|eq|…: value}]}` rules, when the column has them.

hidden.description: Hidden by default in the report.

id.description: The key of this column in each sample's `values`.

namespace.description: The tool the column comes from (`FastQC`).

QcGeneralStats.description: A run's MultiQC General Statistics as data (`GET /runs/{id}/qc/general-stats`).

columns.description: The columns in the report's order.

report_output_id.description: The MultiQC report these come from (an output of the run).

QcSample.description: One sample's General Statistics values, by column id (a missing value is absent).

id.description: The id a form, an example or a submit names it by (`grch38-gatk`).

igv_genome.description:
A genome the alignment viewer hosts (`hg38`, `mm39`) to show this bundle's alignments
against instead of its own FASTA: its sequence and annotation then come from the viewer's
public servers, not from biffix (so set it only for public assemblies).

uris.description:
Named entries → `s3://` URIs (`fasta`, `fasta_index`, `gtf`, `star_index`, …): a file, a
folder (an index directory, its trailing `/` optional), or an index named by its base path
(`s3://refs/hg38/bwa/genome` for `genome.amb`, `genome.bwt`, …), which a submit accepts for
the params the bundle fills.

ReferenceBundleRequest.description: `POST /references` and `PUT /references/{id}` request (on `PUT`, `id` must match the path).

ReferenceUse.description: The reference bundle a run was launched with and the URIs it filled, by bundle key.

RefusedEvent.description: One event of an ingest batch the route refused, by its position in the request.

index.description: The event's index in the request's `events`.

RegisterRequest.description:
`POST /workflows` request: freeze an immutable workflow version. The caller (CI/CLI) supplies
the resolved `git_sha` + `source_content_hash` + normalized `form_schema`.

about_markdown.description:
The version's About page: the Markdown file the manifest names with `about:` (at most
[`MAX_ABOUT_BYTES`]).

form_schema.description: The normalized FormSchema (as produced by the schema→form adapter).

git_sha.description: Resolved commit SHA the version pins.

image.description:
Default worker image: an image reference (pinned to its digest), or a bare `sha256:...`
digest of an image in the deploy's workflow repository.
Optional — omit it when every rule/process declares its own container (Nextflow `container`,
Snakemake's `aws_batch_container_image` resource); the version then carries no default
image.

images.description:
The workflow's named images (`images:` in `biffix.yaml`), each imported into (or built in)
the tenant repository. An imported default image is sent in `image`; a default image built
from the workflow is sent here as `images["default"]` (with `image` left unset — sending
both is rejected).

nextflow_plugins.description:
Nextflow only: the plugins the workflow declares (`plugins:` in `biffix.yaml`), each pinned
by the sha256 of its registry zip. They are built into the version's runtime (the
coordinator runs Nextflow offline), so they are part of its runtime key. Empty for a
workflow that declares none.

queue_classes.description: Worker queue-classes this version's tasks reference (validated against the deploy menu).

registration_inputs.description: How the CLI was invoked, recorded so the version can be re-registered from its inputs.

source_content_hash.description: Deterministic content hash over the source tree.

RegistrationInputs.description:
What a registration was given beyond the source itself (whose `biffix.yaml` travels with it):
enough, with the name, project and source, to register the same version again.

cli_version.description: The CLI release that registered it.

reregistered_from.description: The version this one was re-registered from (`POST /workflows/{id}/reregister`).

source_mode.description: How the coordinator fetches the source: `git` or `s3`.

RegistrationOverrides.description: Command-line values that override or add to the source's `biffix.yaml`.

image.description: The default worker image as given (a tag or digest), before it was pinned.

cached.description:
Already imported or built on this deploy, and for a Snakemake image that is not
`runtime: own`, already derived with the version's runtime: nothing to build for it.

previous_source_ref.description: What the version re-registered from pinned, when it differs.

ReregisterPlan.description: What re-registering a version would do (`dry_run`).

id.description: The version it would register; when `identical_to` is set, nothing would be registered.

identical_to.description: The existing build with the same inputs, when re-registering would change nothing.

runtime_cached.description: The runtime is already built on this deploy.

ReregisterRequest.description:
`POST /workflows/{id}/reregister` — register a version again from what it recorded, on this
deploy's engine runtime, re-pinning its images.

dry_run.description: Report what re-registering would do without registering anything.

engine_version.description:
An exact engine release to use instead of the recorded one (needed for a version that
recorded only a major version, e.g. `9`).

project.description:
The project to register the new version in, instead of the one the version was registered
in: how a version labelled with a project the deploy does not configure is moved into one.

RunCost.description:
A run's estimated AWS cost: compute and root volume for the time each job ran, from its host's
type and AZ and EC2 prices. An estimate, not the bill — it excludes host boot/idle time, credits
and Savings Plans; same-region S3 transfer is free.

estimated_usd.description: Every priced job — all task attempts (retries and spot-lost ones too) and the coordinator.

pending_jobs.description: Jobs not priced yet (still running, or priced on the next reconcile tick).

price_sources.description: The distinct price sources behind the estimate (see [`JobCost::price_source`]).

winning_usd.description:
Only each task's final attempt, plus the coordinator: what the run would have cost without
retries.

RunDag.description: The run's group-level dependency graph for the DAG view: nodes (with rollups) + directed edges.

edges.description: Directed edges as `[from, to]` node-id pairs.

cancelled_by.description:
Who asked to cancel the run (their label), when it was cancelled on request and a label is
known: never an opaque user id.

oneOf.description: The host the coordinator ran on, when known.

coordinator_job_id.description:
The coordinator (head) job's Batch id — links to the coordinator job/logs, the only visible
artifact when a run fails before scheduling any child task.

coordinator_log_stream.description:
The coordinator's CloudWatch log stream (read it through `GET /runs/{id}/coordinator-logs`).
Absent before the coordinator starts.

oneOf.description: The run's estimated cost; absent until a job of the run has run.

dag.description:
The group-level DAG (nodes + edges) with per-node task rollups. Empty when the engine
reported no graph (an engine that does not emit `run_dag`).

engine_session_id.description:
The engine session the run executed as — for Nextflow, the key of its resume cache under
`<output_prefix>.nextflow/cache/<engine_session_id>/`. Absent for Snakemake runs.

input_tables.description:
Samplesheets biffix wrote for this run from rows given at submit, by param:
`{uri, etag, rows: [{column: value}]}`. Absent when none were.

launched_at_micros.description:
When the run's coordinator was launched (its first launch), epoch microseconds: where its
run time starts, as a typical run's (`WorkflowEstimate.typical`) does, so a wait for
submit-time images or in the queue is not counted. Absent before launch.

output_prefix.description:
The run's S3 output prefix (`s3://<project-bucket>/biffix/runs/<run_id>/`), filled by the
handler which knows the deploy's project bucket.

params.description: Resolved params at submit, already secret-redacted. `{}` when none/unknown.

oneOf.description: How `output_prefix` relates to this run. Absent without a prefix.

Where the run's submit-time images are, while it waits for them (`preparing_images`).
Absent otherwise.

What the run ran with (source commit, images, engine runtime), from its submit record.
Absent when the store keeps no event log.

The reference bundle the run was launched with and the URIs it filled, by bundle key:
`{id, uris}`. Absent when none was chosen.

resumable.description:
Whether a `--resume-from` of this run passes the submit path's resume rules (finished,
intermediate files kept, a Nextflow run's session recorded, a prefix to resume in) — the
same check, so a client offers resume exactly when a submit would accept it. The version
being launched must still be of the same workflow and engine.

resume_cache_uri.description:
A Nextflow run's resume cache, `<output_prefix>.nextflow/cache/<engine_session_id>/` (the
coordinator's `cloudcache.path`, keyed by session). Absent without a prefix and a session.

resumed_from.description:
The run this one resumed (`--resume-from`): it shares that run's output prefix, work dir and
engine session.

retention.description:
What happens to the run's intermediate files: `default`, `delete_on_success` or `keep`.
Absent ⇒ `default`.

session_mismatch.description:
True when the engine reported a different session than the one biffix launched it with (so
`engine_session_id` is the engine's own). Omitted when false.

submit_images.description:
The images given at submit (`--image`), as pinned: from the run's anchor once it launched,
else from when it was accepted (so a run that failed while preparing them has them too).
Absent when the submit named none, or the store keeps no event log.

work_deleted_at_micros.description:
When the retention sweep deleted the run's intermediate files (a Nextflow run's `work/`),
epoch microseconds. Its results are kept, but it can no longer be resumed.

workflow_registered_at_micros.description:
When the run's workflow version (`workflow`) was registered, epoch microseconds: with the
git sha the version id starts with, a version label a person can tell apart. Absent when the
registry no longer has the version (or could not be read).

RunDetail.description:
`GET /runs/{id}` detail: the run's summary (flattened onto the wire) plus its task table, DAG,
and resolved (secret-redacted) params.

RunExperimentSetRequest.description:
`POST /runs/{id}/experiment` — put a run in an experiment (of its project), or take it out
(`experiment_id: null`, or blank). Recorded as the run's `experiment_set` event.

experiment_id.description:
Required, even to take the run out (`null`): a body without it (say, a misspelled field)
is refused rather than read as "out of any experiment".

RunFilter.description: Which runs by state: the runs list's filter (`GET /runs?filter=`).

exists.description:
`None` until S3 has been checked; `Some(false)` when the object is gone (a `temp()` file
removed, or deleted since).

id.description: Opaque, stable id; the per-object routes take this, never a key.

last_modified.description: Epoch seconds S3 last modified the object.

modified_since_produced.description:
The object's etag no longer matches the one its producer reported: something (often a later
run sharing the output prefix) has overwritten it.

path.description:
Relative to the run's output prefix when inside it, else the engine's own path, else the
bucket-relative key.

reused.description:
The registering run (this one, or the one named by `reused_from`) satisfied it from the
engine's cache (a Nextflow `-resume` cache hit) rather than producing it.

reused_from.description:
Set when this run registered no output for the file and a run it resumed did: the nearest
run in its resume chain (directly or through others) that registered it, sharing this run's
output prefix. That run is not necessarily the one that wrote the bytes (it may itself have
had it from the cache: see `reused`). Distinct from `reused`: a Snakemake resume skips a
finished task and registers nothing for it, so its file comes from the earlier run's record;
a Nextflow resume registers a cache hit on the resumed run itself, with `reused` set.

role.description: output | published | intermediate | log | benchmark (open set).

servable.description:
Whether biffix will issue a download link for it. False ⇒ listed only (outside the project
bucket, or under a reserved prefix).

size.description: Bytes: S3's answer once checked, else what the engine reported.

viewer.description:
How the UI can show it in the browser: `table`, `text`, `image`, `pdf` or `html`, from the
file name. Absent ⇒ download only.

RunOutputPage.description: A page of a run's outputs, ordered by `s3_uri`.

enrichment_pending.description:
How many matching outputs S3 has not been checked for yet (sizes still unknown). Each list
request checks a bounded number, so re-requesting converges to zero.

next_cursor.description: Keyset cursor for the next page; absent on the last page.

output_prefix.description: The run's effective output prefix, which `path`s are relative to.

total.description: How many outputs match the filter (across all pages).

RunOutputQueryRequest.description:
`POST /runs/{id}/outputs/query` request: the output-list filters in a JSON body. A task key, a
directory and the cursor (an output's S3 URI) can all name a sample or a file, so a client
sends them here rather than in a request URL, which proxies and access logs record.

after.description: Keyset cursor from a prior page's `next_cursor`.

prefix.description:
Only outputs whose path (relative to the run's output prefix) starts with this: a directory
of the output-prefix tree (`qc/`), or a file's own path (`qc/S1.bam`, which also matches
files named after it, such as `qc/S1.bam.bai`: how a client finds one file's output).

roles.description: Roles to include; absent or empty ⇒ every role except `intermediate`; `*` ⇒ every role.

RunPage.description: A page of runs plus the total matching the filter/search (for the list's pagination controls).

first_cursor.description:
Keyset cursor bounding the newer edge of this page — pass as `before` to page back. `None`
on an empty page.

last_cursor.description: Keyset cursor bounding the older edge — pass as `after` to page forward. `None` when empty.

RunPreparation.description:
A run waiting for its submit-time images: each image and where its import is, and why the run
cannot launch yet.

not_ready.description: One line per image not yet runnable.

since_micros.description: When the run was submitted (epoch microseconds).

RunProvenance.description: What a run ran with, as recorded when it was submitted (its `run_submitted` anchor).

git_sha.description: The workflow source commit the run ran.

image_digest.description: The default image the run's tasks ran, pinned by digest. Empty when the version has none.

image_map.description:
Each image reference the workflow declares (as written and normalized) → the tenant image
its tasks ran. Absent when the run recorded none.

image_source_digest.description:
The default image as imported, when the tasks ran an image derived from it (a Snakemake
image with the engine runtime added).

oneOf.description: The engine runtime the coordinator ran with. Absent when the run recorded none.

submit_images.description:
The images given at submit (`--image`), as pinned, from the run's anchor. Absent when the
submit named none (and, like the rest of provenance, for a run that never launched: see
`RunDetail.submit_images`).

RunQueryRequest.description:
Which page of runs to return: the query of `GET /runs`, or the JSON body of `POST /runs/query`.
The body form keeps the search text (which can be a run name, and so name a sample) out of the
request URL, and so out of every access log.

after.description: Keyset cursor: return the next (older) page after this one. From a prior `last_cursor`.

attention.description:
`true`: only the caller's failed runs they have not dismissed (the Lab home's *Needs
attention*; opening or reading one leaves it there). Implies `mine`.

before.description: Keyset cursor: return the previous (newer) page. From a prior `first_cursor`.

experiment.description: Only the runs in this experiment.

oneOf.description:
Which runs by state (default all). A string here, parsed with `RunFilter::parse` once the
caller may list runs: an unknown one is a 400.

ids.description:
Only these runs, by id (at most 200; an unknown id is left out): how a client names many
runs it knows only by id at once (the run folders a Data page lists). Empty or absent ⇒ any
run; a list whose ids are all blank names no run (an empty page, never every run). In the
body of `POST /runs/query` only: `GET /runs?ids=…` is refused with a 400, since a query
string carries no list.

limit.description: Page size (default 50, clamped by the store).

mine.description: `true`: only runs the caller submitted ("my runs"). Default: everyone's.

q.description:
Free-text search: a case-insensitive substring of one of run id, run name, workflow name,
the pipeline's title (its form's `title`), workflow-version id, submitter, submitter label,
project or engine. A name the UI derives for an unnamed run is not searched as a whole, but
its pipeline title is.

workflow.description: Exact frozen workflow-version id to scope to (runs of one registered version).

RunRenameRequest.description:
`POST /runs/{id}/name` — rename a run, or clear its name (`run_name: null`, or blank) so readers
show a derived one. Recorded as the run's `run_renamed` event.

run_name.description:
Required, even to clear the name (`null`): a body without it (say, a misspelled field) is
refused rather than read as "clear". Trimmed; at most 200 characters.

RunReport.description:
One report a run wrote (`GET /runs/{id}/reports`): a report its workflow declared, or a MultiQC
report found among its outputs.

declaration.description:
The 0-based index, in the workflow's `reports:` (`biffix.yaml`), of the declaration this
report came from: the same for every file and sample one declaration produced, so a client
can group by it (two declarations may share a name). `None` for a report no declaration
produced: the undeclared MultiQC report and `detected` FastQC results.

format.description:
How to show it: `html`, `table`, `image`, `pdf`, `alignment`, `reads`, `fastqc` (a FastQC
`_fastqc.html` or `_fastqc.zip`; its data comes from `/fastqc`) or `file` — the author's
`kind:`, else from the file's name. Open.

kind.description:
`declared` (the workflow's `reports:`), `multiqc`: the run's MultiQC report, the one
`/qc/general-stats` reads (found by name; a declared report that is it keeps its name), or
`detected`: a FastQC result the workflow did not declare, found by name (for the QC
previews; a client listing only what the workflow declared leaves these out). Open.

output.description: The output that is the report (open it with the output view/preview endpoints).

sample.description: For a `per_sample` report, the sample this one is (its `{sample}` in the declared path).

RunReportList.description:
A run's reports: declared ones first, in the workflow's order (one declaration's reports
together: a per-sample one sample by sample in the run's sample order, each sample's files back
to back in path order), then the run's MultiQC report, then the FastQC results the workflow did
not declare (`kind` `detected`, `format` `fastqc`, grouped by sample the same way, then any no
sample owns).

RunSampleCounts.description: How a run's samples stand (`biffix_core::sample_progress::SampleCounts` on the wire).

declared.description: Whether the run has a sheet (`false`: `total` is the samples seen so far).

total.description:
With a sheet (`declared`): the sheet's samples plus any other sample a task named; else the
samples tasks have named so far.

RunSubmitRequest.description: `POST /runs` request: launch a frozen workflow version with resolved parameters.

experiment.description:
Launch the run into this experiment (of the version's project); recorded on the run from
birth (`RunSubmitted.experiment_id`).

images.description:
Container images a task may name that the version does not declare (repeatable
references). Each is pinned at submit and imported (and, for a Snakemake version, given
the version's runtime) like a declared image; until every one is runnable the run waits in
`preparing_images`. One wins every spelling it has over a version image spelled the same;
one given with a digest (`ubuntu:24.04@sha256:…`, how a re-run or resume gives its prior
run's images) also wins its spelling without the digest (`ubuntu:24.04`).
An image already imported into the deploy (registered, or named at an earlier submit, as a
re-run or resume of that run does) needs only the role that may launch; one new to the
deploy needs the Developer role, since importing it is what registration does.

keep_going.description:
Submit-time keep-going: whether the rest of the DAG keeps running after a task fails
(Snakemake `--keep-going`; Nextflow has no equivalent and ignores it). Absent ⇒ the
deploy's default (true).

output_prefix.description:
Submit-time output prefix: the workflow's default storage location (Snakemake
`--default-storage-prefix`; Nextflow work/publish dir). Must be within the project bucket and
outside the prefixes biffix keeps for itself (`biffix/runs/`, `biffix/cache/`,
`workflow-sources/`); a trailing `/` is added when missing.
When set, outputs land at this caller-chosen stable prefix — so a series of runs can share
one location and re-run incrementally (Snakemake skips outputs that already exist there),
and downstream tooling finds them where it expects. When absent, falls back to the isolated
per-run `biffix/runs/<run_id>/`. biffix's own run artifacts (events, task records) stay
under `biffix/runs/<run_id>/` either way — only the workflow's data outputs follow this. One
run at a time: a prefix another run is still using (or another submit is launching into) is
a 409.

params.description: Parameter values keyed by FormSchema field name: a JSON object (`null` means none given).

reference.description:
A reference bundle id, for a version whose form has a reference dropdown. biffix fills the
form's reference params from the bundle (replacing any value given for them in `params`) and
refuses a bundle lacking a key the form requires.

resume_from.description:
Resume a previous run: this run re-uses that run's output prefix and work dir, so tasks
whose inputs and code are unchanged are satisfied from what it left (Snakemake from the
metadata the prior run synced there; Nextflow also from its engine session's cache). The
prior run must be a finished run of the same workflow (any version) and engine, and a
Nextflow one must have a recorded session; `output_prefix`, if also given, must equal the
prior run's. A resume is
refused (409) while another run is still using that prefix. The server does not inherit
params: `params` is the complete set (the CLI pre-fills it from the prior run).

retention.description:
What happens to the run's intermediate files once it ends (Nextflow runs only): `default`
(the deploy's retention period), `delete_on_success` or `keep`. Results are never deleted;
deleting a run's intermediate files means it can no longer be resumed. Only a run's own
per-run prefix is ever swept, so `delete_on_success` is refused for a custom `output_prefix`
(or a resume of a run in one).

retries.description:
Submit-time default retry count for failed tasks (e.g. spot reclaims). A default only: a
Snakemake rule's own `retries:` and a Nextflow pipeline's own `errorStrategy`/`maxRetries`
still win. Absent ⇒ the deploy's default (3). At most 10.

retry_of.description:
The run this one tries again (the Lab view's *Try again* re-run; a resume names it in
`resume_from`). Its notification is marked read and dismissed for the caller, so it
leaves *Needs attention*. Must be a run the caller can see.

run_name.description: A human name for the run, shown in run lists and on the run page. At most 200 characters.

tables.description:
Samplesheet rows by param (`{column: value}` per row), for params whose form declares a
samplesheet. biffix validates them, writes the sheet under the run's own prefix and sets the
param to it; a value also given in `params` for that param is replaced.

target.description:
Submit-time target to build (engine-agnostic): a Snakemake target rule/output, or a
Nextflow `-entry` workflow. When set, overrides the version's registered target for this
run; when absent, the version's baked target is used. Lets one frozen version drive
different targets (e.g. a quick `smoke` vs the full `all`) without re-registering. One word
of the engine's command line, so a 400 unless it reads as one target: Snakemake, a rule name
or relative file path (ASCII letters, digits and `_ . - + /`, not starting with `-` or `/`);
Nextflow, a workflow name (an identifier).

workflow_version_id.description: The frozen workflow version id to launch (`{git_sha}:{content_hash}:{build}`).

cost_pending.description:
Whether the run has jobs not priced yet that still can be (its detail's
`cost.pending_jobs > 0`), so `cost_usd` (or its absence) is not final yet, even for a
`terminal` run.

cost_usd.description:
The run's estimated cost so far (USD): its detail's `cost.estimated_usd`, every priced job
([`RunCost::priced_usd`]). Absent until a job is priced (even when the detail's `cost` is
present with only pending jobs). It keeps growing
