until every job is priced, which can be after the run is `terminal`: the pricer prices
finished jobs on its next reconcile tick, and the coordinator only after the run ends (see
`cost_pending`). Also on the run detail, next to its `cost`.

engine.description: Engine (snakemake/nextflow), joined from the workflow version.

experiment_id.description: The experiment the run is in, if any.

input_uris.description: The input URIs declared at submit (provenance; empty when the submit declared none).

outputs_reused.description: Of `outputs_total`, the objects satisfied from the engine cache rather than produced.

outputs_total.description:
Output objects the engine registered for this run, excluding work-dir intermediates. 0 when
the engine registered none.

project.description: Owning project, joined from the workflow version.

resumed.description:
The run resumed another (`--resume-from`), so it may have results it reused from the runs it
resumed though `outputs_total` (what it registered itself) is 0. The run detail names that
run (`resumed_from`).

run_name.description: The run's human name, given at submit or by a later rename (`POST /runs/{id}/name`).

oneOf.description:
How the run's samples stand (the Lab view's "9 of 12 samples done"); absent when no task
names a sample.

tasks_cached.description: Of the succeeded tasks, how many were engine cache-hits (a subset of `tasks_succeeded`).

tasks_cancelled.description:
Tasks the run's cancel ended: still open when it was cancelled, or failed only once the
cancel was requested. 0 unless the run was cancelled.

tasks_observed.description:
Observed task-outcome counts over the projected task rows. Always present (0 when no tasks).
The UI pairs these with `total`: a determinate bar when `total` is known, else an
indeterminate indicator with these as outcome chips (done/running/failed).

tasks_queued.description:
Tasks whose live Batch attempts are all still queued (e.g. `RUNNABLE`, waiting on capacity)
— none has started executing.

terminal.description:
Whether `state` is terminal (the run changes no more), as the server's run lifecycle
decides. A client reads this rather than re-deriving it from `state`, an open string whose
set of values may grow. Filled by the API handler; `false` only means "still in flight" when
the server sent it.

workflow_name.description: The workflow's display name (joined from the version), for a human-readable label + link.

workflow_title.description:
The pipeline's friendly title (the version's form `title`, from `biffix.yaml`), joined from
the version; absent when its author gave none.

RuntimeUse.description: The engine runtime a run's coordinator ran with.

coordinator_image.description: `<repo>@sha256:…` of the coordinator image (base image + this runtime).

SavedReferenceBundle.description:
The saved bundle, with a warning per URI that could not be found (saved anyway: the files may be
on their way).

SiteSettings.description:
`GET /settings` — the customizable site chrome. Both fields optional so an unset deployment
renders defaults. Also the stored row (`SettingsStore`).

logo_data_url.description:
The logo as a raster-image `data:` URL (kept small; checked at the API boundary). `None` =
wordmark only.

oneOf.description:
Who Lab users ask when an analysis needs attention (a pipeline's own `catalog.contact` wins
for its runs). `None` = no *Ask* button.

title.description: Display title shown in the header/tab (falls back to "biffix" when unset).

SiteSettingsUpdateRequest.description:
`PUT /settings` — a partial update. Per field: absent keeps the stored value; `null` or an empty
(or, for the title, blank) string clears it; any other value replaces it.

oneOf.description: `null` removes the support contact. Setting or clearing it needs an Admin.

SourceUploadRequest.description:
`POST /workflows/source-upload` request: ask the backend to presign a PUT for staging a
workflow-source tarball. The client computes the source identity (`{git_sha}:{content_hash}`)
locally — the id the registered version extends with its build number — so the staged object is
content-addressed and can be uploaded before the `POST /workflows` call.

context_tree_hash.description:
Stage an image build's context instead of the source: the content hash of the context's
files (64 hex), which names the tarball beside the source.

project.description:
The project the version is registered in, whose bucket the tarball is staged into. A
deploy of one project stages into it whatever this names.

version_id.description:
The source identity (`{git_sha}:{content_hash}`, a version id without its `:{build}`) the
source is staged under. Every build registered from this source shares it.

SourceUploadTarget.description: `POST /workflows/source-upload` response: where and how to upload the tarball.

headers.description:
Headers the PUT must send as given (the URL's signature covers them). A source's PUT is
write-once (`If-None-Match: *`): a version runs whatever its staged key holds, so a staged
source is never replaced, and a 412 means this source is already staged there. A build
context's PUT has none (its build checks the tarball's sha256).

uri.description: The `s3://` uri the object lands at — record this verbatim as the version's `kind:s3` source.

url.description: The presigned URL to PUT the `source.tar.gz` body to (plain HTTPS; no AWS creds needed).

StartedUpload.description: A started upload: send `parts` parts of `part_size` bytes (the last may be shorter).

uri.description: Where the file will be (`s3://<project bucket>/<key>`).

StatusHistory.description: `GET /status/history` — bucketed uptime history for the status page's bars.

bucket_secs.description: The bucket width in seconds (the client builds a fixed timeline from this + `window_secs`).

expected_per_bucket.description:
Samples expected per full bucket at the 5-minute probe cadence. Only a tenant running a
workflow samples that often, so whether a bucket is covered is read from its samples'
promises ([`UptimeBucket::covered_until`], [`UptimeBucket::lapsed`]), not from this count.

grace_secs.description: How long past its promise a sample still counts, in seconds (the grace `GET /status` allows).

window_secs.description: The full window span in seconds.

StatusReport.description: `GET /status` — the worst tier across `components`, plus each component's own tier.

SubmittedImage.description: An image given at submit: the reference as written and the digest-pinned source it resolved to.

SubmittedRun.description:
`POST /runs` response: the new run's id and state, plus its coordinator job / assumed role once
it has launched.

assumed_role_arn.description: Absent while the run is preparing images.

coordinator_job_id.description: Absent while the run is preparing images.

state.description: `submitted` (launched now) or `preparing_images` (waiting for its submit-time images).

SupportContact.description: A person (or team) to ask for help: the site's support contact, or a pipeline's own.

url.description: A help page (a ticket form, a chat channel), shown beside the email when set.

Task.description: A task row within a run's detail.

cached.description: Whether this (succeeded) task was an engine cache-hit rather than work run this time.

cost_usd.description:
Estimated cost of every priced attempt of this task (USD), retries and spot-lost attempts
included; absent until one is priced.

deps.description:
Task keys of the tasks in this run that this one depends on (produced its inputs). Its
inverse is `feeds`, which only `POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query` fills: a reader of
`GET /runs/{id}`'s whole task list derives it from the list.

exit_code.description:
Per-task display detail from the task's display attempt; omitted when absent (a local rule,
or an attempt that has not terminated yet).

feeds.description:
The run's tasks that depend on this one (the inverse of `deps`). Filled by
`POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query`, which pages tasks and so cannot leave the inverse to the
client; empty in `GET /runs/{id}`'s task list.

group.description: The DAG node (rule/process) this task rolls up onto, when known.

oneOf.description: The host the display attempt ran on, when anything about it is known.

image.description:
The container image the task ran in (its display attempt's), as the engine reported it at
submit; absent when the engine did not report one.

requested_memory_mib.description: The memory (MiB) the display attempt's Batch job requested; absent when unknown.

requested_vcpus.description:
The vCPUs the display attempt's Batch job requested (not its host's capacity — see `host`); absent when
Batch reported no requirement.

spot_warned_at.description:
When EC2 warned that the display attempt's spot host would be reclaimed (epoch seconds), if
it did while the attempt was running.

started_at.description: Attempt start / finish as epoch seconds.

verdict_reason.description:
Why the workflow engine failed this task although its AWS Batch job did not fail (e.g. it
did not write its declared outputs); absent otherwise.

TaskAttempt.description:
One AWS Batch attempt of a task. A task retried after a spot reclaim has several; `Task`
summarizes only the display attempt (the succeeded one, else the highest-numbered).

attempt.description: The engine's attempt number (1-based); absent until the engine's submit is observed.

oneOf.description: The attempt's estimated cost, once priced.

display.description: Whether this is the task's display attempt (the one `Task` summarizes).

oneOf.description: The host the attempt ran on, when anything about it is known.

instance_id.description: The ECS container-instance id of the host (not an EC2 instance id).

queue.description: The Batch job queue (name) the attempt ran on.

requested_memory_mib.description: The memory (MiB) the attempt's Batch job requested; absent when unknown.

requested_vcpus.description:
The vCPUs the attempt's Batch job requested (not its host's capacity — see `host`); absent when
Batch reported no requirement.

spot_warned_at.description:
When EC2 warned that the attempt's spot host would be reclaimed (epoch seconds), if it did
while the attempt was running — i.e. the attempt was lost to a spot reclaim.

started_at.description: Attempt start / finish as epoch seconds.

state.description:
The attempt's own last observed state: created, submitted, queued, running, succeeded or
failed.

status_reason.description: Batch's human-readable reason for a failed attempt.

TaskAttemptList.description:
`POST /runs/{id}/attempts/query`: every attempt of one task, ordered by attempt number
(unnumbered last), then Batch job id.

TaskAttemptsRequest.description:
Which task's attempts to return: the JSON body of `POST /runs/{id}/attempts/query` (the task key
kept out of the request URL).

TaskFilterCounts.description: Task counts by the Jobs tab's filter chips, over the tasks matching the other filters.

TaskLogsRequest.description:
Which page of one task's log to return: the JSON body of `POST /runs/{id}/task-logs/query`. A
body keeps the task key (whose wildcards name a sample) out of the request URL, and so out of
every access log.

cursor.description: Opaque CloudWatch cursor from a prior page (`next_forward_token`/`next_backward_token`).

direction.description: `forward` (live-tail toward newer events) or `backward`/absent (tail — newest first).

job.description:
One attempt's Batch job id (from the task's attempts); absent ⇒ the task's display attempt.
Must be an attempt of this task of this run, else 404.

limit.description: Max events to return (default 200, clamped to 1..=1000).

TaskPage.description: `POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query`: one page of a run's tasks.

counts.description: Counts per state filter, with the group and search filters applied.

log_group.description:
The CloudWatch log group the tasks' `log_stream`s are in, when it is not the fleet-wide
`/aws/batch/job`: a run's tasks log to their project's task log group. Omitted ⇒
`/aws/batch/job`. (A run launched before its project had that group logged to
`/aws/batch/job`; the log routes fall back to it, a console link built from this does not.)

total.description: Tasks matching every filter, across all pages.

TaskQueryRequest.description:
Which page of a run's tasks to return: the JSON body of `POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query`. A body
keeps a search term or a task key (which names a sample through its wildcards) out of the
request URL, and so out of every access log.

order.description: asc (default) | desc: `desc` reverses the sort's natural order.

q.description: A substring of the task key.

oneOf.description:
Which tasks by state (default all). A string here, parsed with `TaskStateFilter::parse`
once the caller may see the run: an unknown one is a 400.

task_key.description:
Only the task with exactly this key (e.g. a linked task, which a substring search can bury
under the many keys that contain it).

TaskStateFilter.description:
Which tasks by state: the Jobs view's filter chips (the `state` of
`POST /runs/{id}/tasks/query`).

TypicalRun.description:
A typical run of a workflow: the median wall time of its recent successful runs, and their
median cost when at least two of them are priced.

hours_median.description: Median hours from launch to completion.

runs.description: Past runs the times are from.

usd_median.description: Median USD of the priced ones; absent with fewer than two priced.

UnreadCounts.description: The reply to a read: the caller's unread counts after it.

UploadCompleteRequest.description: `POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/complete`: assemble the file from its parts.

project.description:
The project whose bucket the upload is in; absent ⇒ the deploy's default project. A deploy
of one project uses it whatever this names.

UploadKeyRequest.description:
`POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/status` and `/abort` request: the upload's object key, in the
body so a file name never reaches a request URL or an access log.

project.description:
The project whose bucket the upload is in; absent ⇒ the deploy's default project. A deploy
of one project uses it whatever this names.

url.description: A presigned `PUT` URL, valid for 15 minutes; the response's `ETag` header names the part.

project.description:
The project whose bucket the upload is in; absent ⇒ the deploy's default project. A deploy
of one project uses it whatever this names.

UploadStartRequest.description: `POST /data/uploads`: start a resumable upload into the project bucket.

key.description: The object key in the project bucket; must be under `uploads/`.

project.description:
The project whose bucket the upload is in; absent ⇒ the deploy's default project. A deploy
of one project uses it whatever this names.

UploadStatus.description: `POST /data/uploads/{upload_id}/status`: the parts already uploaded, to resume.

UptimeBucket.description:
One bar of a component's uptime history: how many probe samples in the bucket saw each tier,
and how far past them their promise of the next sample runs.

The probe samples every 5 minutes while a coordinator is active but only hourly on an idle
tenant, and each sample promises the next within its `next_within_secs`. A bucket is covered
when none of its samples came later than the sample before it promised (plus
[`StatusHistory::grace_secs`]) and its newest sample's promise runs to the bucket's end; an
empty bucket after it is covered while that promise runs, at that sample's tier.

covered_until.description:
Epoch seconds by which the bucket's newest sample promised the next one, before the grace (a
sample written before samples carried a promise is held to the hour).

lapsed.description:
A sample in the bucket came later than the sample before it promised, plus the grace, or had
no sample before it within the hour: the probe missed part of the bucket.

last.description: The tier of the bucket's newest sample.

t.description: Bucket start as epoch seconds (aligned to the bucket interval).

UsageReport.description: Estimated spend over a period (`GET /usage`), from EC2 prices.

total.description: The whole period (each run counted once).

runs.description:
Runs with a cost estimate submitted in the period (by instance type, a run on several types
counts in each).

UserPrefs.description:
`GET /me/prefs` — the caller's own display preferences. Also the stored row (`SettingsStore`).
A user with no stored row gets the defaults: no view chosen (the UI shows Lab), nothing pinned.

pinned_workflows.description:
Pinned pipelines, in the order the user pinned them. Each is an opaque key the client
chooses (the UI stores `JSON.stringify([project, name])`), not a workflow name: the server
only trims, de-duplicates and caps them.

tour_done_at.description: When the user finished or skipped the first-visit tour (epoch seconds); `None` = not yet.

oneOf.description: `None` until the user picks one (the UI's default is `lab`).

UserPrefsUpdateRequest.description: `PUT /me/prefs` — a partial update. Per field: absent keeps the stored value.

pin.description:
Pin one key (opaque to the server, see [`UserPrefs::pinned_workflows`]), atomically against
the stored list: appended when absent (the order kept), a no-op when already pinned.
Trimmed; 1 to 512 characters. A pin past the cap of 50 is a 400 and stores nothing. At most
one of this and `unpin` per update (400 otherwise).

tour_done.description: `true` records the tour as done now; `false` clears it (replay the tour).

unpin.description:
Unpin one key, atomically against the stored list; a no-op when it is not pinned. Trimmed;
1 to 512 characters.

VersionRelease.description:
Whether a version is released now, and by whom: the one release shape every workflow read
carries (`GET /workflows`, `GET /workflows/{id}`, `PUT /workflows/{id}/release`).
`at_micros`, `by` and `by_label` describe the change that released it, so they are set only
while `released`.

at_micros.description: When it was released, epoch microseconds.

by_label.description: A human label (email/name) for who released it, when it could be resolved.

VersionRuntime.description: A version's engine runtime and its coordinator variant for the deployed base image.

builds.description: How many builds of the variant there have been.

coordinator_image.description: The image a run launches on now (`<repo>@sha256:…`).

ready.description: Whether a run can launch now (on that variant, or on one built on an older base image).

recipe.description: Every pin the runtime is built from (`engine`, `engine_version`, `pins`, …).

state.description: The variant for the deployed base image: `unbuilt` | `building` | `failed` | `ready`.

ViewMode.description: The run view a user picks: the biologist-facing Lab view or the full Expert view.

WorkflowEstimate.description:
`GET /workflows/{id}/estimate?samples=N`: a launch's cost and time from the workflow's recent
successful runs. `estimate` is absent until it has two runs with a cost and a sample count.

oneOf.description:
How long (and how much) one run of the workflow usually takes, whatever its sample count:
from its recent successful runs, sample count or cost recorded or not. Absent until it has
two. Answered with or without `samples`.

WorkflowImage.description: One of a version's images and where its import is.

arch_builds.description: A built image's build per architecture.

capabilities.description: What the import found in it (`bash`, `libc`, `snakemake`).

declared_ref.description: As declared (a built image: its name).

derived_image.description:
The image tasks run when it is derived (a Snakemake image with the version's engine runtime
added: `<tenant workflow repo>@sha256:…`), once derived.

derived_state.description:
The derive's state (`unbuilt` | `building` | `failed` | `ready`), for a derived image whose
import is done.

generated_dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile biffix generated to build it (a `pixi` image).

image.description: The imported image (`<tenant workflow repo>@sha256:…`), once imported.

kind.description: `import` (an existing image, imported), `dockerfile` or `pixi` (built from the workflow).

reason.description: Why it cannot be used (a failed import or derive, or an image unsuited to the engine).

source_ref.description:
Pinned at registration: `<registry>/<repo>[:tag]@sha256:…`; a built image: what it is built
from (`dockerfile:docker/align/Dockerfile`, `pixi:envs/worker`).

WorkflowListing.description: A workflow's listing, as stored (`PUT /workflows/listing` response).

updated_at_micros.description: When it was last set, epoch microseconds.

updated_by.description: Who last set it (actor id); absent when unknown.

WorkflowListingUpdateRequest.description:
`PUT /workflows/listing` request: hide (or show again) a workflow on the Lab's pipeline cards.
Applies to every version of the (project, name). A curator's setting, unlike the author's
`catalog:` block.

name.description: The workflow's name (may contain `/`, hence the body rather than the path).

WorkflowRelease.description:
A version's release in full (the `PUT /workflows/{id}/release` answer): whether it is released
now, every release and un-release of it, newest first, and whether the caller may change it.

can_change.description:
Whether the caller may release or un-release it (a Developer or Admin). A hint for the UI;
the `PUT` is authorized on its own.

history.description: Every change, newest first; empty for a version never released.

release.description: Whether it is released now (from the newest change in `history`).

WorkflowReleaseChange.description: One release or un-release of a version, as recorded (never changed afterwards).

by_label.description: A human label (email/name) for who, when it could be resolved.

WorkflowReleaseUpdateRequest.description:
`PUT /workflows/{id}/release` request: release a version, or (`false`) take the release back
so it is a developer version again.

WorkflowVersionDetail.description:
`GET /workflows/{id}` detail: the full frozen version, including the `form_schema` the CLI
validates params against.

about_markdown.description: The version's About page (Markdown), when it has one.

build.description: The build number among versions frozen from this same source (0 for the first).

can_release.description:
Whether the caller may release or un-release it (a Developer or Admin). A hint for the UI,
like [`WorkflowRelease::can_change`]; `PUT /workflows/{id}/release` is authorized on its
own.

created_at_micros.description: When this version was registered, epoch microseconds.

created_by.description: Who registered this version (actor id captured at registration); absent when auth is off.

created_by_label.description: A human label (email/name) for the registrant, when it could be resolved.

form_schema.description: The normalized FormSchema (opaque JSON — the CLI/UI deserialize it via `biffix-workflow`).

image_repository.description: ECR coordinates of the frozen image (for a console deep-link); absent when unknown.

images.description: The version's images and where each import is.

not_ready.description: Why the version cannot run now (empty when ready).

registration_inputs.description: What the registration was given beyond the source.

retention_days.description:
The deploy's retention period for a run's intermediate files (a Nextflow run's `work/`), in
days after the run ends, for the launch form's choice. Absent ⇒ they are kept forever
unless a run asks for deletion on success. Filled by `GET /workflows/{id}`.

oneOf.description:
The engine runtime the version's pinned release is built into (absent when the version's
readiness could not be read).

state.description:
`ready` (it can run) | `pending` (its runtime or an image is still being built) |
`failed` (one failed; see `runtime` / `images`). Absent when its readiness could not be
read.

oneOf.description:
How the version is listed in the Lab's pipeline catalog; absent when there is nothing to
say. A form with no `catalog:` block still gets one when the server can say what a run gives
or takes (`results`/`inputs`), so its presence does not mean the author declared a catalog.

created_at_micros.description: When this version was registered, epoch microseconds.

created_by.description: Who registered this version (actor id captured at registration); absent when auth is off.

created_by_label.description: A human label (email/name) for the registrant, when it could be resolved.

hidden.description:
Hidden from the Lab's pipeline cards (`PUT /workflows/listing`), set for every version of
the workflow's (project, name). The Expert list still shows it. Read from the workflow's
listing in `GET /workflows` and in a registration's (or re-registration's) response alike.
Distinct from `catalog`, which is the author's, frozen with the version.

image_repository.description: ECR coordinates of the frozen image (for a console deep-link); absent when unknown.

last_run_at.description:
When the newest run of this exact version was submitted, epoch seconds; absent when it has
none (or in a registration's response).

release.description:
Whether this exact version is released (`PUT /workflows/{id}/release`): a Developer or
Admin promoted it; every other version is a developer version. Per version, unlike
`hidden`. A registration's (or re-registration's) new version is never released.

run_count.description: Number of runs launched from this exact version (joined from the runs projection).

state.description:
After a registration: `ready` | `pending` | `failed` (see `GET /workflows/{id}`). Absent in
lists.

summary.description: A one-line summary: the form's description, else the first sentence of the About page.

title.description:
The pipeline's friendly title (its form's `title`, from `biffix.yaml`); absent when the
author gave none, and the name is the title.

oneOf.description:
How long (and how much) one run of the pipeline usually takes, as
`WorkflowEstimate.typical`: from the recent successful runs of its (project, name), any
version. Set in `GET /workflows` for every version of the pipeline alike (so a catalog asks
no more); absent until two such runs, and in a registration's response.
